flawed_step: Lines 0026-0038 (Part 2 inductive step), especially 0028-0032: 'The endpoints of P lie in H and are colored, say, red and blue (since H is bipartite)' and 'this cannot happen because the boundary of the new face created by adding P must be an even cycle'.
counterexample: Take G = the 3x3 grid graph: vertices (i,j) for i,j in {0,1,2}, edges between grid neighbours. G is 2-connected and plane; its faces are the four unit squares (4-cycles) and the outer 8-cycle, so every face boundary of G is an even cycle, i.e. G satisfies the hypothesis of Part 2. Now run the proof's induction. Start with H = the outer 8-cycle (0,0)(1,0)(2,0)(2,1)(2,2)(1,2)(0,2)(0,1). Add the ear P1 = (1,0)-(1,1)-(1,2) (length 2, interior vertex (1,1) not in H). (a) Refutation of line 0031-0032: adding P1 creates two new bounded regions of H' = H + P1, the left one bounded by the 6-cycle (0,0)(1,0)(1,1)(1,2)(0,2)(0,1) and the right one by the 6-cycle (1,0)(2,0)(2,1)(2,2)(1,2)(1,1). Neither is a face of G -- the edge (0,1)-(1,1) of G lies strictly inside the left region and the edge (1,1)-(2,1) lies strictly inside the right one; in fact G has no 6-face at all. So the hypothesis 'every face of G is an even cycle' says nothing whatsoever about the region created at this stage, and the proof's only justification for the ear's parity is void. (b) Refutation of line 0028-0030 as literally stated: continue with the ear P2 = the single edge (0,1)-(1,1), which has odd length 1. Its two endpoints (0,1) and (1,1) get colours 1 and 0 under the proper 2-colouring of H' by the parity of i+j, i.e. different colours, so H' + P2 is still properly 2-coloured and no monochromatic edge appears. This contradicts both the assertion that an ear's two endpoints are automatically coloured 'red and blue' (in the same run, the ear from (1,0) to (0,1) along (1,0)(2,0)(2,1)(2,2)(1,2)(0,2)(0,1) has both endpoints the SAME colour), and the assertion that an odd-length ear forces a monochromatic edge. The parity bookkeeping in lines 0029-0037 is therefore incorrect, and after removing it nothing in the argument rules out an odd ear: the proof never establishes the fact it needs (that every cycle of a plane graph is a mod-2 sum of face boundaries, so all cycles are even once all faces are even).
reasoning_summary: Part 1 is fine (every cycle of a bipartite graph is even). Part 2 is where the proof breaks. Its induction adds ears to a subgraph H and claims the parity of each new ear is forced because 'the boundary of the new face created by adding P must be an even cycle' -- but the regions created at intermediate stages of an ear decomposition are not faces of G, so the hypothesis about G's faces does not apply to them. The explicit 3x3 grid instance shows a stage whose new regions are 6-cycles while G has no 6-face (edges of G lie strictly inside those regions). The supporting colour argument is also stated falsely: it claims the two endpoints of an ear are coloured red and blue because H is bipartite, and that an odd ear forces a monochromatic edge; in the same grid, the ear (0,1)-(1,1) has odd length 1 with differently coloured endpoints and extends the colouring fine, while the ear (1,0)-(2,0)-(2,1)-(2,2)-(1,2)-(0,2)-(0,1) has both endpoints the same colour. With the false parity rule removed, the induction has no mechanism to exclude an odd ear, so Part 2 is not proved. The theorem itself is true, but this proof of the converse direction is invalid.
counterexample_target: the claim that the region created by adding an ear is a face of G (hence even), and the claim that an ear's endpoints receive different colours / that an odd ear forces a monochromatic edge
